opportunities.title: Small grants

amount.raw: Awards generally fall in a range of £1,500-£5,000 and will only exceptionally exceed £6,000. Travel and subsistence in Japan up to £2,000 per person for trips up to 13 days, up to £2,500 per person for trips of 14 days or more; up to £5,000 for PhD fieldwork visits of six months or more. Japan office considers awards up to ¥300,000 for PhD students from Japan.

opportunities.eligibility_summary: Applicants must belong to, or provide evidence of support from, an organisation or institution willing to receive grant funds. Applications are not accepted from individuals seeking support for personal projects, though the UK office may consider individuals with proof of organisational support. Payments cannot be made to personal bank accounts.
opportunities.summary: Seed funding to enable UK-Japan projects that might otherwise not be possible, bringing people in the UK and Japan together to deepen mutual understanding, exchange ideas or expertise, or develop lasting collaboration. Supports festivals, workshops, performances, exchanges, collaborative projects, Japanese language teaching, and academic research/visits.

opportunities.title: Butterfield Awards in Medicine and Health

deadlines.raw: 1 December (annual, for decision in March of the following year)

amount.raw: Up to £10,000; continuing projects lasting up to three years to a maximum of £10,000 per year, to a total limit of £30,000.

opportunities.eligibility_summary: Applicants should normally be able to show an existing research record, but consideration is also given to practitioners, managers, carers or others in health-related fields. Projects must involve partners in both the UK and Japan. Preference given to those not previously involved in UK-Japan collaboration and early-career applicants. Apply to the UK office regardless of where based.
opportunities.summary: Supports exchanges and collaborations between health and medical professionals in Japan and the UK, including study of scientific, clinical, social and economic issues in healthcare. Creates opportunities for researchers, practitioners, policy makers, managers and voluntary sector workers to share knowledge and develop new approaches. Grants may be used for travel expenses or other costs including conference and publication costs.
